headline: Expect a weak, nervous start. Oil eased overnight, but Infosys's US shares fell 6.6% after a forecast cut, Asia is lower, and every trend check still points down.

mood.label: Negative
mood.why: All 4 direction checks point down (bias −66), but bets on a fall are very crowded. Overnight data as of 08:48 IST.

key_points.text: Infosys's US shares fell **6.6%** after it cut its yearly sales forecast. Indian IT stocks react today.
Brent crude is down **1.8%** since India closed, to about $114, but still near its yearly high.
My call: a slow drift lower is more likely than a bounce, with **low-to-medium** confidence.
FIIs hold about **9 bets on a fall for every 1 on a rise** in index futures. That can flip into a sharp bounce on good news.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: Slightly worse for the open: cheaper oil helps, but weak IT and Asia extend last week's slide.

points.text: GIFT Nifty (Nifty traded overnight) was about **22,595** at 7:23 am, almost flat vs Friday's 22,600.
Asia is down: Korea **−1.3%**, Japan −0.8%. US futures are up only 0.2%.
Brent is down **1.8%**, the dollar down 0.2%, and the US 10-year rate eased to 4.97%.
Infosys's US shares fell 6.6% and Wipro's **3.7%** on Friday, pointing to IT selling at the open.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: I lean to a mild fall or a flat, choppy day, not a strong bounce. Confidence: low-to-medium.

points.text: Bounce signs: FIIs are only **10.4%** long in futures, near the under-10% zone where they often buy back. The put-call ratio (bets on a fall vs a rise) is 0.81, near the gloomy 0.7 mark.
Fall signs: on Friday price fell while futures positions rose 1.3%, meaning **new bets on a fall**. Friday's fall (0.39%) was no panic, so there is little to reverse.
I'm wrong if Nifty climbs back above **22,715** (its 20-day average) and holds, or oil drops below $110.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is down on every check, but Nifty is near the bottom of its recent range.

points.text: Nifty at 22,600 is below its 20, 50 and **200-day** averages, with lower peaks and lower dips.
Four straight falls from 23,146. The October low of **22,232** is the next level to watch.
India VIX (the fear gauge) at about 16.8 is higher than on **78%** of days this year: expect bigger swings.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: FIIs keep selling and betting on a fall; Indian funds keep buying more.

points.text: FIIs bought a small **₹888 crore** on Friday, only their third buying day this month.
For October, FIIs have sold **₹37,283 crore** of shares.
Domestic funds (DIIs) bought **₹43,887 crore** this month, which is why the fall is slow, not a crash.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Costly oil and a possible US rate rise are India's two biggest worries.

points.text: Brent is up **13.7%** in a month on Iran fears. India imports about 85% of its oil, so this lifts prices and weakens the rupee (94.94 per dollar).
Fed decides late Wednesday (India time). Betting markets see a **hold** at about 93%, but US bill rates suggest a rise later, probably December.
The US 10-year rate is near **5%**, which pulls money away from markets like India.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Mixed results; Infosys is today's main story.

points.text: Infosys: profit up 6.3%, 'in line' by the dashboard's rule, but it cut its yearly growth forecast to **1–2%**. The US share fall shows the market disliked it.
Dr Reddy's profit fell **32%** (Weak); JSW Steel's rose 226% and Shriram Finance's 59% (Strong).
Tata Consumer reports today; **L&T, Maruti** and Tata Steel tomorrow.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: A packed week: expiry, the Fed, and many results.

points.text: Tuesday 3:30 pm: **monthly expiry** of Nifty options, so expect sharp swings.
Thursday around midnight IST: **Fed decision**. A surprise rise would hurt India.
Iran: a strike could send oil up; calm news could bring **oil down fast**.

levels.note: A close above 23,000 would mean a real bounce; below 22,000 the fall could speed up.

watch.text: How Infosys and IT stocks open.
Whether Nifty holds 22,500 or slips toward 22,232.

bottom_line: The dashboard is clearly bearish: all 4 checks point down, FIIs are betting heavily on a fall, and oil is near its yearly high. Overnight news is a little worse, mainly Infosys and Asia, partly offset by cheaper oil. My read is a weak or flat day, with low-to-medium confidence. The main risk: FIIs rushing to close their one-sided bets on good oil or Fed news.
